messages.author: e044c18cfaaee0c7
messages.subject: Passing a list to a function
parts:
Hi all,
I need to calculate the average value of and increasing area.
I have a  coordinates file: MESHTRIA.TXT. which has in the first column node number, second column x coordinate and y coordinate in the third column.
As the area increases, I need bigger number of nodes for the average.
After finding the nodes I need in this file, I need to extract their value from the other file: "TH.TXT" and average them.
I tried to use "lapply" to calculate the average value for all the areas I need but it gives me  "NULL" answer.
I'm guessing I made a dumb mistake somewhere but I can't figure out where.
Any help?

nodes_tot <- read.table ("MESHTRIA.txt", sep = "", nrow = 1)
number_of_nodes <- nodes_tot[[2]]
mesh <- read.csv ("MESHTRIA.txt", sep = "", skip = 1, nrows = number_of_nodes, col.names = c("node", "x", "y"), header = F)
dia10 <- mesh[mesh$x <= 5  & mesh$y >= 42 & mesh$y <= 50, 1]
dia20 <- mesh[mesh$x <= 10 & mesh$y >= 42 & mesh$y <= 50, 1]
diameter   <- list (dia10 = dia10, dia20 = dia20)

theta <- read.table ("TH.txt", sep = "", header = F, skip = 1, fill = T)
time_data <- as.numeric (row.names (theta [theta$V1 == "Time",]))
run_time <- theta [time_data, 3]
wc <- data.frame(matrix(NA, nrow = length (run_time), ncol = length (diameter)))


wc_calc <- function (diameter) {
      for (i in 1 : (length (time_data) - 1)) {
            a <- theta [(time_data [i] + 1) : (time_data [i+1] - 1),]
            aa <- na.omit (as.vector (as.matrix (t (a))))
            wc$diameter [i] <- mean (as.double (aa [diameter]))
            }

}
wc <- lapply (diameter, wc_calc)

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Passing a list to a function
parts:
It is always good to learn some debugging tools when you start writing functions - Duncan Temple Lang with the DSI has put up some pretty good resources.

In this cause, you are running into issues with scoping. You are calculating a value inside of a for-loop, but not recording it anywhere. This works as intended:

wc_calc <- function (diameter) {
    ans = numeric(length(time_data)-1)

for (i in 1 : (length (time_data) - 1)) {
            a <- theta [(time_data [i] + 1) : (time_data [i+1] - 1),]
            aa <- na.omit (as.vector (as.matrix (t (a))))

ans[i] = mean (as.double (aa [diameter]))
    }
    return(ans)
}



That said, there are much better ways to do this calculation - the function above relies on Global variables (things in your environment), which can be a huge source of bugs. Additionally, for loops are very slow in R, and we tend to try to write vectorized code when possible.

messages.author: a2bfdf24157fa01a
messages.subject: Re: Passing a list to a function
parts: Have you verified that the code above is actually working correctly? I am a bit confused by what you are referring to as "nodes" and "coordinates", etc., but I have a feeling that these lines are not doing what you think they are:
aa <- na.omit (as.vector (as.matrix (t (a))))
wc$diameter [i] <- mean (as.double (aa [diameter]))

In particular, how do you know that "diameter" is indexing correctly into your data that has been transposed, collapsed into a vector column-wise, and then cleaned of NAs? If there are any NA values, the correct index into "aa" will shift, so you will pull out different values depending on whether or not there are NAs.  I would check that you are getting the correct answer before worrying about making it more efficient.

Assuming your "node" is the position row-wise of the value you want according to:

1 2 3 4
5 6 7 8
...

then the "node" x resides in column:

x%%n_column#(where 0 means in column n_column

and in row:

ceiling(x/n_column)

Therefore, you can get your indices of interest with:

rows = ceiling(dia10/ncol(theta))
cols = dia10 %% ncol(theta)
cols[cols == 0] = ncol(theta)

of_interest = cbind(rows, cols)


Now, you just subset your matrix by this. Other tricks: your time_data are evenly spaced (unique(diff(time_data))), so you can just calculate how far you need to jump from each starting point. 

To put it (mostly) altogether: (Disclaimer - I am pretty sure this works, but I did not test it thoroughly. Make sure you verify before using.)

# using dia10 
rows = ceiling(dia10/ncol(theta))
cols = dia10 %% ncol(theta)
cols[cols == 0] = ncol(theta)

of_interest = cbind(rows, cols)

start = time_data + 1
jump = unique(diff(time_data)) - 1

foo = function(start, jump, theta, of_interest)
{
    sapply(seq_along(start), function(i, start, jump, theta, of_interest){
        a = theta[start[i]:(start[i] + jump),]
        tmp = as.numeric(as.matrix(a)[of_interest])
        mean(tmp, na.rm = TRUE)
    }, start, jump, theta, of_interest)
}


You should also wrap the part to convert from the "node" to row,col in a function.

messages.subject: Re: Passing a list to a function
parts:
These files are a result of a numerical model simulating water and solute transport in soils using a finite element mesh (triangles in this case). The nodes are the intersections between the mesh elements and have values calculated in them. Since I'm interested in only specific areas in the simulation (but can't simulate only that area) I'm filtering for these nodes. The size of the matrix and the time steps change with each simulation so between files nothing stays the same,..except the NA's which are always at the end of the file and the number of columns in the "TH.TXT" file. That's why I tried to write the code as general as possible.
I have checked that the code works and I'm getting the right answers. I couldn't figure out how to filter for different ares (which you solved), plot the mean with time for all areas, and next how to run this for all files in all directories..
